rule: Dark-band width measured with the fine ruler (rows[].fine). The brightness profile across the trace is walked as by the earlier, coarser ruler, with two changes: every pixel of the target layer is a sample (no stride) and the profile step is 0.25 px (s = arange(-R, R + 0.125, 0.25)); the half-depth crossings are interpolated linearly between neighbouring profile samples, which gives a continuous width. Ring part, centre part, the rule that a depth below 2 grey levels has no dark band, and the median are unchanged. Self-check in the same code path: the coarse ruler (every 4th target pixel, step 0.5 px, width (hi - lo) x 0.5) is computed again on every row (old_ruler) and must equal apparent_width_px of b_summary_formal.json exactly (old_check, old_ruler_check). Inputs: the cases of b_cases.json whose role is not scale; the label layers (label_dir) and the image frame.png (png) of each frame; pixel_mm from the camera and the camera plan. Resolution check: the samples are split by their row-major index in np.argwhere(target) modulo 4 (k = 0..3) and the median is taken per subset. group_2: per camera, the change of the median width from a mean opening of 3 cm to 8 cm over the expected change in pixels, with its verdict on the full set and on each subset; resolved is true when the five verdicts agree. monotonic: at the 6 viewpoints of the dark-band width table, whether the median width never decreases with the mean opening (base 5.5 cm = row b055 of the camera), on the full set and on each subset, with the decreasing steps listed. criterion: name and SHA-256 of the file that lays down this procedure and its checks; module_sha256 and analyze_opening_sha256: SHA-256 of the script of this measurement and of the script of the coarse ruler; these three files are not part of the package. The numerical libraries ran with one thread.
